key_insight: This paper proposes estimating a partner’s hidden capabilities so an AI agent can adapt to new collaborators without assuming a fixed task or perfect partner behavior. In simple terms, the agent learns what its teammate is likely able to do, then uses that estimate to coordinate more effectively.
problem_solved: Ad-hoc teamwork methods typically assume the task is fixed and the partner’s abilities are already known. This paper addresses the real-world problem of collaborating with unknown, diverse, and sometimes sub-optimal partners across tasks with multiple valid strategies.
method: Estimate partner capability from observed behavior rather than assuming it is known in advance.
Use these estimates to support task-agnostic adaptation, enabling the agent to adjust coordination across different tasks.
Account for human-like variability where partners may choose sub-optimal actions even when the overall task can be solved in multiple ways.
impact: This is useful for AI systems that must cooperate with humans or unfamiliar agents in open-ended settings. It can improve robustness, flexibility, and coordination quality in real-world multi-agent and human-AI teamwork.

paper_title: Partner Capability Estimation for Task-Agnostic Adaptation in Ad-Hoc Teamwork
paper_authors: Peter Tisnikar, Maja Swieczkowska, Benteng Ma, Gerard Canal, Matteo Leonetti
